brief.recommendation: Checkout success is 39% vs 95% SLO with $11,244/min revenue at risk (BIZ-3). The blocker (adhoc_reporting) has been idle for 25.8s (DB-3) of the 60s tolerance window (BIZ-3). The workload has no registry entry (BIZ-2), making interrupt cost unknown (BIZ-4). No active change-calendar window exists (BIZ-5). Per I4, unknown workload cannot be priced for termination. Per I7, waiting risks exceeding the 60s tolerance. Per I3/I4, this trade-off belongs to the human owner. Escalation is the correct action.

audit.report: On 2026-02-10, the checkout service degraded after an unknown workload acquired a lock on session pid 152929 (batch_worker/adhoc_reporting). The blocker ran a trivial SELECT 1 for 25.8s, during which checkout success dropped to 39% (vs 95% SLO), putting $11,244/min in revenue at risk. Both guardians recommended waiting, but the Continuity Guardian invoked a business invariant after 25.8s, arguing that continued degradation exceeded the 60s tolerance window. The Database Guardian proposed escalation, and the case was escalated to an on-call human before a terminate-or-wait decision was finalized.
audit.root_cause: An unknown workload (adhoc_reporting) held a lock on session pid 152929, blocking checkout sessions and causing checkout success to fall to 39% within 25.8s.
lessons: Register adhoc_reporting in biz.workload_registry immediately so the cost of interrupting it can be quantified before a lock-contention incident recurs.
Add adhoc_reporting to the protected-settlements list (or define an interrupt_policy) so the Continuity Guardian can evaluate termination without invoking the business-invariant override.
audit.negotiation_critique: The guardians correctly identified the blocker and quantified revenue risk, but the Continuity Guardian’s invariant override short‑circuited the R2/R3 wait proposals after 25.8s, preventing a potentially safe wait within the 60s tolerance. The Database Guardian lacked registry data to estimate interrupt cost, which forced the invariant check to fail.
follow_ups: Populate biz.workload_registry for adhoc_reporting with owner and estimated runtime.
Define interrupt_policy or protected-settlement status for adhoc_reporting to allow termination evaluation without invariant override.
Review the 20s watchdog timer design with the on-call team to ensure it aligns with the 60s business tolerance.
